utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Registrar, perhaps first there were some dossiers that need still to be given numbers. Could you please name them and name their numbers as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The first one is the Bijeljina municipality dossier which will be given prosecution exhibit P801. The next one would be the Ilijas municipality which will be P802. The Prijedor municipality dossier will be given P803. The [Realtime transcript read in error: "Rogota"] municipality dossier will be given P804. And the Sokolac [Realtime transcript read in error: "Kolak"] municipality document will be given P805.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to avoid any misunderstanding, Rogota should be Rogatica and Kolak will be Sokolac. Yes. Mr. Stewart, are you ready to continue the cross-examination of Mr. Prstojevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then in terms of time, examination-in-chief took five hours. The Judges have taken quite some time as well. The cross-examination -- you thought, Mr. Stewart, that you would need approximately three hours. One of the concerns of the Chamber is that cross-examination by both counsel and some additional questions by the accused should not lead to any further consumption of time. Therefore, the Chamber would very much like to see that you arrange or you cross-examine the witness in such a way, perhaps after brief consultation with Mr. Krajisnik, that we would be in a position to finish cross-examination at the first break, which would be approximately five quarters of an hour from now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- because I'm afraid I haven't done the calculation but I know the Trial Chamber knows this kind of thing, but how long have I had so far?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two hours, Mr. Stewart. Could the witness be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, before the witness comes into the courtroom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- first of all, it is a point I have made in relation to a number of witnesses. When one has a witness with such a very large series of interviews, a long series of interviews, even though those interviews are not of course in accordance with Your Honour's ruling themselves part of the witness's evidence in the form of a statement, but that itself indicates that it's very likely that that witness will be a witness with a 60 per cent guideline, which is only a guideline, that should be flexibly applied. And Your Honour knows that overall the Defence are comfortably one the 60 per cent guideline and taking one witness with another. And the whole point of that guideline, we submit, is that there are witnesses where it's suspected and it's appropriate and in fact it's achieved that the Defence would be well within the 60 per cent guideline and there are witnesses where quite legitimately because of the substance of the evidence we would be over the guideline --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, I'm going to stop you here. It's not on the basic which you seem to suggest, not on the basis of the 60 per cent guideline. We asked you at the beginning how much time you would need. You said it would be approximately three hours. Apart from that the Chamber also takes into consideration the way and the subjects and the time and the -- how the witness is cross-examined. Let's not spend ten or more minutes on discussing this matter. Let's bring the witness in.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must protest --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: When the Court asks me for a time estimate, I will not give one in future if I'm going to be subject to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- what is tantamount to a trick, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, I want you -- I have put your microphone off at this moment. Mr. Stewart, it's not a trick. This Chamber is not playing tricks. I just responded to your suggestion that it was the 60 per cent guideline which was guiding this Chamber. I said that more elements were taken into consideration, among which what you said. Let's start with the further cross-examination of the witness. The witness may be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, how am I to resolve the position with Mr. Krajisnik? There is an important point here. Your Honour knows the difficulties to Mr. Krajisnik. Your Honour knows quite frankly that I have not voluntarily willing in any way to give any time to Mr. Krajisnik in relation to cross-examination because Your Honours know that I regard the opportunity that you have given to the lay client to ask questions on cross-examination, Your Honours know that I regard that as an intrusion on my conduct of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that, Mr. Stewart. At the same time, it's not -- where you say that you give any time to Mr. Krajisnik, this Chamber considers all the time spent on cross-examination as time spent on the Defence of Mr. Krajisnik. It's not the one who gives time to the other; it is a way of finding a solution for how to address matters which you find important, matters that Mr. Krajisnik find important, in such a way that the cross-examination will be most effective. I suggest --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, you're taking the conduct of the case out of my hands, which is entirely inconsistent with the whole basis of which counsel takes over a case of this nature and inconsistent with the code of conduct and inconsistent with the proper practice, Your Honour. I really must protest at what the Court is doing. My co-counsel would not be permitted by me -- would not expect by me -- to take without proper consultation with me and without my full agreement and approval because I and my co-counsel assisting me have conduct of the case. Your Honours are putting me in the position where I'm overridden by my own client's wishes and overridden by the Tribunal. And having the conduct of the case and my judgements -- and my judgements as to what time is needed and what cross-examination should take place taken away from me, Your Honour, which is absolutely an improper way, in my submission, of dealing with the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber heard your observations. We'll now continue with the cross-examination of the witness, and you're invited to consult with Mr. Krajisnik to see whether he has any questions to be put to the witness and how much time he would wish, which is not the same as how much time he could spend on putting those questions to the witness. If you'd like to do that, you have an opportunity now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, there is a problem with that which is Mr. Krajisnik is generally not willing and with respect to him is generally not able either to say until my cross-examination is completed because it is only when I've completed my cross-examination -- does Your Honour not see, with respect, the huge problems created here. I cannot sensibly discuss with my client in advance any timing. I cannot have discussion ss as I could with co-counsel because Mr. Krajisnik considers the right as he considers my cross-examination is inadequate, as lay clients do whether it is or it isn't, whether he considers me not to cover the ground to cover ground himself. So we never know, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, if -- we'll consider the matter. You may consider cross-examination of the witness, Mr. Prstojevic, and this Chamber will try to find solutions for the problems which within the Defence cannot be resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Prstojevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, and good morning to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. You'll now be further cross-examined by Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Stewart: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, good morning. I should say very frankly --

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should say from where I'm standing -- from where I was sitting, I can -- of course I cannot read the words, but I can see that you have brought your notebook with you and I can see that you have reasonably extensive notes. May I invite you to confirm, Mr. Prstojevic, that you have not added anything to your notebook since court finished on Friday until you came into court this morning.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have. I jotted down a few things I was thinking. First I recalled the name of the technical secretary, the first and last name of the technical secretary in the Municipal Board of the SDS. Her name is Biljana Cabak. The other day I only knew her first name. Now I'm adding the last name. The administrative worker, the other day I could remember that her name was Mila, but her last name is Mila Cakar. Also, I recalled that the secretary of the Crisis Staff until the 4th of April, 1992, was Ignac Simic, the secretary of the SDS Municipal Board. After the 4th of April, 1992, this was done by Mr. Momcilo Ceknic who was the secretary of the municipal office. The other notes are of a private nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prstojevic, I'm sorry to probe you on this, but they're of a private nature but relating to this case, are they?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they don't. If I jotted down my dream on Saturday night, that has nothing to do with the trial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Mr. Prstojevic, perhaps we can short-circuit this. Will you turn over to a new blank page. Just put everything you've written in the book -- thank you for your helpful piece of information on the secretary. Could you just make sure that everything you've written is shut up in front of you and start with a blank page. Is that okay? Thank you. Mr. Prstojevic, I'm going to ask you about -- it's page 46 of the transcript of your interview. You were asked about the meeting which you say you attended and you were asked by Mr. Mitford-Burgess: "Was it mandatory for you and the officials from Ilidza to attend?" And you say: "Obligatory, of course." Why did you tell the interviewers that it was obligatory when according to the evidence you've given to this Court, it plainly was not obligatory for you?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we were invited to certain meetings in writing or by telephone, we were obliged to attend. If we were not invited to attend a meeting, then we were not permitted to attend unless we received permission to do so at our own request.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I want to ask you then about something you said on Thursday, which was about the subordination of the Crisis Staff, your Ilidza Crisis Staff, to the president of the Serbian Assembly. And you were asked: "Is it correct" -- this is page 5, line 8: "Is it correct, Mr. Prstojevic, that the Serbian Crisis Staff of Ilidza was subordinated to the president of the Serbian Assembly?" And your answer was: "The Crisis Staff at Ilidza was basically set up and operated in line with the instructions I saw here." And then you said: "It's quite clear the responsibility of the Crisis Staff had to do with the fact that they were accountable to the state and political bodies that issued those instructions and asked for them to be implemented. Basically coordinating activities of the Crisis Staff would be subject to consultations and agreement with the top political and state leadership." Mr. Prstojevic, does all this and what else you've said mean that it isn't correct to say that the Crisis Staff of Ilidza was subordinated to Mr. Krajisnik, as it was at the time, as president of the Serbian Assembly?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by what I said before. The state political leadership -- actually, the president of the People's Assembly is at the top of the state political leadership. So it is understood that the Crisis Staff and the war commission were subordinated to the national or the People's Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, when you were interviewed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The president of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were interviewed, and this is page 48, Mr. Margetts said to you: "So as president of the Crisis Staff of Ilidza, you were subordinated to both Momcilo Krajisnik and Radovan Karadzic?" And your answer was: "The assumption is that practically I was, because Crisis Staff at one time had certain functions, certain positions that belonged to the orders of the government."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me, but there's a -- that exchange follows a longer exchange that addresses directly the issues counsel's referring to, beginning with the question: "So did you understand that the Serbian Assembly of Ilidza and the Serbian Crisis Staff of Ilidza was organisationally subordinated to the president of the Assembly?" And the answer: "Absolutely. That's why it reported to it," and so on. So to extract the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, if Mr. Stewart wants to put an emphasis on small portions of the interview, you of course can ask for the context of those portions of the interview to be tendered into evidence so that the Chamber can have a look at the context in which it was said because I do understand that there might be a problem if you just quote one or two lines and take it out of the context. You are entitled to do so. But at the same time, Mr. Stewart is entitled to -- well, perhaps to cut out certain portions. Whether -- to what extent that assists finally the Chamber, to take matters out of context, is of course another matter, but he's entitled to do it the way he wants and you're entitled to add the context to his questions so that the context is in evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Your Honour. My concern on this occasion, as it has been on previous occasions, is not the matter of focussing on a particular portion and asking a witness to clarify any aspect of that, but to the possibility of misleading a witness into thinking that that that was all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would say that entitled to add the context to the evidence. At the same time you're also entitled, if you really take the position that the way certain parts are cut out, that you ask the specific attention of the Chamber to the context so that the Chamber is well aware on whether or not there would be any misleading of a witness. You understand what I mean - so that attention is focussed on it and if it really comes to -- not on just emphasising on certain parts but real misleading, which requires a lot, then of course you may object to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour, and by the use of that term I wasn't suggesting there was any purposeful of that. My point was that when you say to someone this is what you said and it only contains a portion, there is a risk of that possibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. A risk of misleading is not enough. That is the situation but you can add the context. You may draw the attention of the Chamber to it. If there's really misleading of the witness, then you can object.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it will require a lot before I ever infer that Mr. Tieger is accusing me of deliberate misleading. We don't normally have that. Your Honour, since this point is likely to arise from time to time, may I make my position briefly clear in line with what the Chamber has said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: All this on the basis on which the Trial Chamber has ruled, all this material is in evidence in the sense that it has been said by this witness in his interview. Do -- the Chamber has all this material, so it has the context and can always read the questions and answers given by the witness in the light of the context in these interviews. Consequently, what I'm only seeking to do - and I have to do it within the time constraints as well, of course - I'm likely to take the minimum medium context which is consistent with the question not being misleading. But, Your Honour, of course I accept, and it happens from time to time inadvertently when counsel is dealing with a matter -- when a question is suggested to be unfairly misleading as put without a little bit of extra context, then of course I'll respond to that straight away. But the point -- and this is taking a bit of time -- but the point of this question I'm about to ask the witness is not, I'm going to submit, not in the least bit misleading from not including extra lines of context. Those are there and can always be argued in due course. I take the chance, Your Honour, if I give the witness a slightly smaller context, I take the chance on his answer, if it's favourable to me, otherwise being slightly reduced or undermined by the ability of the Trial Chamber in the due course to look at the wider context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The position is clear. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, what I'm urging you to do, please, by way of a question is to indicate not in theory as a matter of political structure but in practical terms, in what way can you say from your own knowledge the Ilidza Crisis Staff was subordinated to the president of the Assembly, in practical terms.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, is that the totality of your answer, Mr. Prstojevic? It seems my question may not have been clear. Are you going on to supplement your one-word answer?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can add to it. However, it is quite clear, according to the instructions, that the Crisis Staff in emergency circumstances, extraordinary circumstances, assumed the duties and obligation of Ilidza's Municipal Assembly, that it is a body analogous to the local Assembly and the government. As such, not only in theory but also in practice, it was coordinating its everyday work with all the state and political bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, can you tell the Trial Chamber specifically of any instruction or order or direction received by the Ilidza Crisis Staff from Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not be able to tell you that at this time. Different persons were in charge of coordination: The president of the Crisis Staff, members of the Crisis Staff, and the secretary of the Assembly who was in charge of coordinating activities with the organs from the Assembly, and that was my virtue of his office. However, quite undoubtedly at a later stage we from the commission and the War Presidency had to provide the president of the national Assembly - that is, the national Assembly of Republika Srpska - with written reports. And this was to take place as soon as the administration became operational and started working at a normal pace. Therefore, we were following the activities of the president of the national Assembly and the national Assembly itself, and they were of course following and evaluating our work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, do you say that at any point the Crisis Staff of Ilidza, the SDS Crisis Staff, had an obligation to report to the president of the Assembly as the primary or main person to whom it was to report?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not have such an obligation at all times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did it have such an obligation at any time?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had the obligation to do so at different meetings, over telephone calls, and through certain ministries. These were the various Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. channels through which the activities and the security and political situation at Ilidza were followed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Mr. Prstojevic, your Crisis Staff never had an obligation to report mainly to Mr. Krajisnik as the holder of the office of president of the Assembly, did it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have given quite an extensive answer to such a question already. I believe I've already answered the question. I keep being asked to say something that is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, do you say that the Ilidza Crisis Staff, first of all, ever received any written instruction from Mr. Krajisnik, coming from him as president of the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the instruction for the operation for the activities in extraordinary circumstances, 093 that we received at the Assembly of Republika Srpska, is quite telling, where we first elected the Municipal Assembly of Ilidza, its president, the secretary, and then we adopted some decisions. The first thing we did was to send a written document to the president of the national Assembly, and I have seen that this Tribunal and the OTP have the documents. You can see that the document was delivered to the president of the national Assembly and you can see that that particular copy is the one that belonged to the president of the Assembly. One can see that by the various markings. Had it not been our obligation to deliver that document, we would not have done so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which document are you talking about there?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the document -- I believe it's the 0093 document, instructions for the activities in extraordinary circumstances, pursuant to which the Crisis Staff and the Ilidza Municipal Assembly were elected and established, and it was according to these instructions that the Municipal Assembly, the government, and the Crisis Staff had to function.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Are you saying that the document that was delivered to the president of the national Assembly is the one which we now see numbered 0093? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to say that pursuant to the document 0093 we established a Crisis Staff, we established the Ilidza Municipal Assembly, and it was pursuant to this document that both these bodies operated. What we did on the 2nd and 3rd January, 1992, was to immediately send a written report to, among others, the president of the Assembly. These documents that we sent to the president of the Assembly, his personal copies I myself had occasion to see in the OTP -- with the investigators. It was both the investigators and Mr. Krajisnik who had them, and I believe also this Honourable Trial Chamber has one copy of that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you said that what you did on the 2nd and 3rd of January was to "immediately send a written report to, among others, the president of the Assembly," who were those others?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We sent the key documents concerning the establishment of the Assembly, the elected functionaries, and two or three decisions that the Assembly adopted on that first day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, that was precisely not my question. I did not ask you what you sent. You have already talked about that. I asked you to whom. When you said it was sent to Mr. Krajisnik, among others, I'm asking you who those other people were, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- these included the Executive Board and the Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, at page 46 of your interview, you -- there was a whole context talking about this document, an example of which you see numbered 93. And you were asked by Mr. Mitford-Burgess: "Being specific here, do you actually know who the individuals were that were commissioned to be authors of this document?" And your answer was: "Ask Mr. Krajisnik. You asked me this and I told you." Now, I'm just going to say -- before I ask you the question I'm going to say I can't find where in this interview you told the interviewers, but if it's there no doubt it will emerge. But now asking you the very small question Mr. Mitford-Burgess asked you, but please do not answer it by referring back to a previous answer. I'm asking you what you say now. Be specific. Do you actually know who the individuals that were commissioned to be authors of that document?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what -- which team of people drafted this document, but I believe that Mr. Krajisnik did know that and that's why I said that he was the person to be asked that question. And this applies to you as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, you were asked at page 6 of your evidence given on Thursday, last week, Thursday, the 16th of June -- what had been put to you was page 184 of your -- the transcript of your interview where you'd given an answer in relation to who comprised the War Presidency of Pale and you said: "President Karadzic, Biljana Plavsic, president of the Assembly, Momcilo Krajisnik, president of the government, whether minister of defence or not, I do not know." First of all, the simple question is you do not know reliably who was in the War Presidency, do you, Mr. Prstojevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. I do not know reliably, but I assume that the case was as I indicated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your answer was: "Precisely because we got no written document telling us who was in the War Presidency, we knew that on the basis of what we'd been told, on the basis of our conversations and assumptions. So I can't tell with 100 per cent certainty that President Karadzic would have been there, although he should have been. So I stick to my previous assessment." Now, Mr. Prstojevic, just for clarification, when you said: "I can't tell with 100 per cent that President Karadzic would have been there," that was a slip, you meant to say that: "I can't tell with 100 per cent certainty that President Krajisnik would be there." Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to all of them. It did not apply only to Karadzic but to all the others that I could not claim with 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, Mr. Prstojevic, I'm going to make clear to you because I am entitled to just explain to you simple facts. You named a particular person in that answer. You said: "I can't tell with 100 per cent certainty that President Karadzic would have been there, although he should have been." First of all, Mr. Prstojevic, then it is clearly 100 per cent certain that President Karadzic would have been included in any such Presidency, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you said: "I can't tell with 100 per cent certainty that President Karadzic would have been there, although he should have been," I'm just suggesting to you that you obviously -- it was a slip, you obviously intended to refer to Mr. Krajisnik there.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't a slip of the tongue. I was talking about Mr. Karadzic. However, now when I'm saying about this percentage, what I'm saying about the percentage could apply more to Mr. Krajisnik, whether he was or was not a member of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to a meeting on the 17th of April. You made a reference to that at page 46 of Thursday's transcript, the 16th of June. You also made a reference to it on the Wednesday, the previous day, the 15th of June, at page 54. You said -- on the Wednesday first you said: "I" -- you said there were -- at the foot of page 53 you said: "There were two more significant meetings attended by the representatives of the armed forces. One was held at Jahorina and the other at Famos. At Jahorina all brigade commanders in the area of Serb Sarajevo were present as well. As to other meetings of different nature or of lesser scope, I think there must have been somewhere from seven to ten." And His Honour Judge Orie said: "This is 1992, is that a correct understanding?" And you said: "Yes, I can only be precise and specific if I can check my papers and I did say before and I'm going to remind you again that at Ilidza I believe on the 17th of April there was a meeting of the part of the government at the Crisis Staff and the meeting was about analysing the security and the political situation and the possibility of having the government of the Serb part of Sarajevo there and the representatives of the government headed by Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik were there, and all the Ilidza representatives headed by myself were there as well." So that -- from that answer, can you confirm. The whole point of that meeting, you say, was to make a decision about where the -- where the headquarters or at least an important part of the headquarters of the Serb government would be located from then onwards. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the meeting held at the Ilidza Crisis Staff on the 17th of April, I thought that the main emphasis was on the security situation in Ilidza. Within the topic of the security situation, the seat of the government and the state bodies of the Serbian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina was also discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, is this right: The reason why such matters had to be discussed was only because in some way Ilidza was, if you like, a candidate to be the location of the Serb government.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. To put it simply, up to that point the Serbian government had not had a seat of its own. It was scattered about and people did not know where other people were located. I don't know why Presidents Karadzic and Krajisnik decided to hold this particular meeting at the Ilidza Crisis Staff; perhaps because we were able to guarantee some level of security at that particular point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, I wonder if you could be given the very document that has been mentioned quite a number of times, 00 -- the one bearing the number 0093, the one that has come to be called variants A and B. Obviously I'm inviting you to be given the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I don't know what's the most convenient exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have many copies --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, we do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I don't mind which one the witness has, if it can be -- it was item --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, two things, Your Honour. First, it's P43, and as the Court noted other -- it bears other exhibit numbers, but it was also item 1 of the exhibits that were distributed in the course of this examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely right, Your Honour, whichever is most convenient. It's P43, it's P64, whether that's part of the larger exhibit. Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I've got a completely clean copy, Your Honour, of the Serbian version which came to course of this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it, Mr. Tieger, you would not oppose of a copy of Mr. Stewart to be used at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, not at all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then we can swap over in due course, Your Honour. That is the item 1 that was handed out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, do you -- how long is it since you have looked at this document or a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In November 2003, I had occasion to look at parts of it and a couple of days ago. It would be good if I had the entire document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I think you have got the entire document, Mr. Prstojevic. You've certainly got the entire Serbian version of the document which was produced earlier in the course of your evidence. Mr. Prstojevic, I'm going to proceed on the basis you have got the entire document because I'm really rather confident that you have. If you look at -- first of all, you do seem, Mr. Prstojevic, to have become slightly confused about whether it's variants A and B, variant A or B. The can we take it that in your municipality you -- your evidence is that so far as you applied this document, you intended to apply whatever was appropriate for a municipality in which the Serbs were in the majority?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what we were intending, but as far as I can recall we were working in accordance with variant B. But I think it doesn't really matter whether it was one variant or the other. We could apply either one in view of the fact that the executive -- that the president of the executive council, the prime minister, was a member of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, which do you say you did apply, Mr. Prstojevic? Because they -- you can take it from me they are not the same. If you can't say which you applied, then tell the Trial Chamber that.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I stand by what I said in the previous statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm going to proceed on the basis that what we get out of his previous statements and statements is variant A and not waste time on the alternative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, can we take variant A, first level. Do you see that? It's under Roman -- immediately under II. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 1: "Introduce round-the-clock duty service in all SDS municipal boards." Well, did you do that in the Ilidza Municipal Board?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this is completely identical in variant B also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't worry about variant B for the moment, Mr. Prstojevic. Did you introduce round-the-clock duty service? You said yes. Is that what happened? Well, did you?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when --

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right away, immediately the following day after we came because this was finished in the evening. At the Assembly, we implemented it immediately, the following day, once we came to Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 6: "Strengthen the service, providing security for public buildings of vital importance in the municipality." Did you do that straight away?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't do that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 7 --

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was understood that companies had their own internal security and that this was under the jurisdiction of the MUP in a way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 7: "Establish control over and check the state of existing commodity reserves and proceed to complete and replenish municipal commodity reserves." Did you check the state of existing -- well, were there commodity reserves, first of all?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, there were no municipal reserves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did --

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the joint government in the previous period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take steps to build up municipal commodity reserves with raw materials and manufacturing components?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't because the president of the Executive Board was our man. We didn't do anything for this particular item.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 10, did you "advise all Serbian staff that they must not go on annual leave, travel abroad, or leave their place of permanent residence in the coming period?"

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to answer this. This document was completely read at a meeting of the SDS Municipal Board, and all the deputies during the formation of the Assembly of the Serbian people of Ilidza, which means that the people's representatives, the political and parliamentary representatives were informed. However, we did not insist, especially on this, because in the early part of the year, January, February, March, and April, is not a part of the year when holidays are used. At that time there was no travel abroad by our people. So there was no need to do anything on this matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that -- this is at page 77 of the transcript on Tuesday, the 14th of June. You talked about another meeting held in -- of a military security nature held before the 1st of April, a meeting which you said you had not been present but you've talked to people who had attended. And then at the top of page 77, line 3: "They told me that some people from the leadership of the party, they told me the names but I don't remember them now, they told me that some people were either militant or excessively optimistic saying we would find it very easy to defend ourselves from the Muslims and if any armed conflict would break out, we would have beat them without any problem, which according to our assessment and their assessment was not true. And they were dissatisfied and as said in my statement, going into conflict with such ideas we could get into bloodshed and it was completely uncertain which would win." Now, you said "according to our assessment and their assessment," and you said it was not true that you would defeat the Muslims without any problem. Who is they -- when you say "in their assessment," who are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was thinking of the assessment of the state political leadership of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that just presented to you or described to you by the people who did attend the meeting in very general terms?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They described it, but not in detail. There was a characteristic manner. A couple of our people were not satisfied with that meeting, so I basically recall extreme or negative instances or incidents. That's what I recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that in Ilidza the units of the Territorial Defence had been mobilised earlier than -- and you're talking about earlier than April 1992, because the formal -- this is page 17 of the transcript of the 15th of June, "because the formal official in charge of Ilidza before the war was in his proper position and everything functioned well." Who were talking about there, the formal official in charge of Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I didn't say that units were mobilised before April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who was the formal official in charge?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And secondly, it's true. In the pre-war municipal government, the joint one of the Muslims, Croats, and Serbs, the head of the TO staff was Captain Dragan Markovic, who was a candidate of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You -- at page 37 and 38 of the transcript on the 15th of June, which was last Wednesday, you talked about Mr. Tomo Kovac. And then at the foot of that page you said: "However, there is one point which is incorrect here that is to say they went to request that -- they were invited to carry out a task which had been determined as early as the 14th of April, that is to say to carry out an attack on certain facilities, amongst other things the ethnic settlement of Ilidza. And the Chief of Staff of that army, Bosnia-Herzegovina, made that decision." Who is the Chief of Staff that you're referring to there?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now I have to look into my notebook so that I just don't speak off the top of my head, if you permit that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can I just ask you please, Mr. Prstojevic, look in your notebook to find notes made when?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noted down a few days ago, and I have it jotted down in different places. We had that dispatch in April. I don't know who sent it to us in Ilidza, whether it was our intelligence service, the JNA, or some representative of the international community. On the 14th of April, 1992, the commander of the TO staff of Bosnia and Herzegovina, it doesn't say here --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you -- if you're saying you don't --

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name I think was Hasan Efendic. It's known who the commander of -- in any event, he ordered the attacks on the JNA barracks, storehouses, ammunition storage facilities, the MUP. And in -- along the Sarajevo-Ilidza-Hadzici axis. And we happened to be on that axis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to a meeting held at the Famos premises in Pale. You said that was a meeting where Mr. Krajisnik was present as well. When do you say that meeting was?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting was held in 1992 when the war was already raging. And I would locate that meeting around the activities of the import of peppers into the Muslim part of Sarajevo by Mr. Danilo Veselinovic who was in charge of logistics for the MUP. But as far as the exact date of the meeting and all of that, unless my diary has been destroyed, I would Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. have that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you say it was before or after the meeting on the 17th of April that was under discussion a short while ago here this morning?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was much later, between that meeting at the Famos premises and this one on the 17th of April, there was the Jahorina meeting and a whole series of minor meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "much later," do you mean many weeks or many months?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that meeting perhaps took place sometime before the end of September 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you say was the purpose of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already talked about that in detail a few days ago, and I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prstojevic, do you mind just answering my question. What do you say was the purpose of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can speak as much as you like, if you want, but I would just be tiring this Court. I think the key thing would be the military and the security situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, who summoned that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our leadership from Pale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to say specifically who summoned it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot say that specifically because I don't know from which cabinet we were invited. It was either from President Karadzic's or President Krajisnik's cabinet, but I'm not sure which one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Karadzic, Dr. Karadzic, at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he hear the meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he did. It was either he or Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say -- I'm not inviting unless you do know to say exactly, Mr. Prstojevic, but can you say roughly how many people were at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the presidents of the municipalities of the Serbian city of Sarajevo were present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's --

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that General Mladic was present and I also think that the brigade commanders were there, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's ten municipalities, was it? Mr. Prstojevic, if you'd say it might be 11 or it might be 9, it's about 10 municipalities, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Less, because Trnovo at the time was part of Ilidza in the organisational sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. So how many people were at the meeting altogether? 15? 20? 30? 40?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really speculate, but they were two, four, six, seven -- seven municipalities. Because seven -- seven, eight, nine -- there were nine municipalities. Trnovo at the time did not exist as a municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't say whether it was 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 people present. Is that right, Mr. Prstojevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. I really cannot guess.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you understand when you attended to be the main purpose of your presence there?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main reason was the agenda of the meeting because all the people were there from nine municipalities who were carrying out these functions, the president of the Assembly, the president of the Executive Board, and I don't know whether the party presidents were also there or not. And then you can see immediately if all the three structures were present, the first two were present, times nine how wrong it would be to speculate on how many people there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What was the -- what was the subject which you understood you were there to deal with, either by contributing to the meeting or by listening to what others contributed? What subject matter -- what were you there for, did you understand?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that. The political and security situation, which includes completely everything that was important for the conduct of war in these municipalities of the Serbian people. And that is why the bearers of the most responsible functions were invited.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the meeting last?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did it -- was it an all-day meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I cannot remember. Sometimes it would last -- well, as I can see it here, it can go on from 4.00 p.m. until 11.00 p.m., but I really cannot speculate on how long the meeting lasted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember anything about the -- any topic of discussion in relation to your municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can remember that and I think that you have that in my previous statements in 2003 or on the 6th of May of this year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Trial Chamber now, please, Mr. Prstojevic, what you can remember, if anything, that was specifically discussed at that meeting relating to your municipality.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A lot of it had to do with the municipality of which I was president as well as with other municipalities. I remember a negative example of the import of peppers by the aforementioned person to the Muslim part of Sarajevo. So I remember that particular incident in detail because the people in Ilidza criticised that. They believed that this endangered our security. It was not clear to them why somebody was importing peppers. They were suspecting all kinds of things, and I criticised that. And I said in my statement in detail how I criticised it, who didn't let me speak anymore because President Karadzic left at one point and they said, Wait, wait, let Mr. Karadzic hear this. So then I continued once Mr. Karadzic returned to the meeting. There's no need for me to repeat all of this now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, I was going to say, Your Honour, I have tailored my cross-examination in accordance with the Trial Chamber's directions, and therefore I have finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Stewart. Mr. Krajisnik, would have any questions to Mr. Prstojevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have prepared a series of questions, but I think that we must resolve the basic question between Mr. Stewart and myself. And on this occasion, I will not ask my question until the question is resolved of how long each one of us can question the witnesses. I would not like to place the Chamber into an uncomfortable situation where I am grabbing to myself the time needed to question the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, the Chamber will pay attention to that issue, but you'll have now an opportunity to put questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. Could the usher please distribute these copies to the Chamber. I have prepared for each of the Judges and for the Prosecutors copies of documents that Mr. Prstojevic will look at and which will be the basis for my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try to be as efficient as possible and to take up as little time as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Krajisnik. Cross-examined by Mr. Krajisnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question of the so-called A and B variant. First I would like to greet Mr. Prstojevic.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would like to extend my greetings to you as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The A and B variant. I would like to ask you, you have the document number 2 in front of you. It's from the back, actually. I have marked the documents in red ink, so this is document number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I remind the Trial Chamber that this portion is from Mr. Grkovic's diary, who was Mr. Karadzic's secretary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document is at the back.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have found the instructions. And which is the other document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says: "Friday, 20th December, 1991."

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then it's the one in front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked about you being unable to remember when this meeting was held. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My questions will be brief. Could you please give brief answers likewise so we can finish this as soon as possible. You didn't know which meeting that was. It wasn't quite clear to you?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I forgot. I believe it was the session of the Assembly of the SDS. In part it was an electoral session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The second page of that same document at the bottom of the page. It is SA043906.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see at the bottom it says "subota"?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is an Assembly of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, it says the Assembly of the Serbian at 12.00, Holiday Inn. Is that what it says here?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at document number 3. It -- you go -- you're going from the back towards the beginning of the binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which seems to be the stenographic notes of the 21st of December, 1991, meeting of the --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of the Assembly of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you for your assistance, Your Honour, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you read that part?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please read it for the record, Witness. Is this the Assembly of the Serbian people at Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back to document number 2. Can you see what it says at the top, 1600 hours?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please read it out to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "1600 hours, Main Board, deputies' club."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. At the bottom of the page it says also "1600 hours."

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Main Board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The next page it says "Monday." Can you read what it says at the beginning here.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At 1800 hours the Main Board. The club of the SDS deputies Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please read there, does it say under Monday?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that this material was distributed during the session of the Assembly of the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe we can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you stated that the material was merely distributed?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only stated that it was distributed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Please look at document number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to remind the Honourable Trial Chamber that it was at this time that the variants A and B were distributed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please read the passage which says -- or rather, the ninth paragraph which is in handwriting. If I may assist you, it says: "The Assembly decision."

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Assembly decision, 26th of December" --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, please. I will read it out and I will ask you to confirm this. "The decision of the Assembly of the Serbian people has arrived from Srebrenica. The deputy of the Serbian municipality." Can you read that? It is written by hand.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The decision of the Assembly of the Serbian people has arrived from Srebrenica." I can see it says here -- or about the establishment of the Serb municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to remind the Trial Chamber that one witness, Mr. Deronjic, testified to this and that the deputy of the Assembly was Mr. Zekic. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, you're not allowed to comment. You may put questions to the witness. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at document number 4. This is the decision on the establishment of the Serb municipality of Ilidza. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 2 under Roman VII, please read that part, would you.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The functionaries, the leaders, and other officials of Serb ethnicity working for the Ilidza municipality, the Executive Board of the municipality of Ilidza, and other municipal bodies and administrative bodies shall continue performing their duties, tasks, and obligations to which they were appointed, elected, or assigned."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what the instructions, or rather the variants A and B include?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember, but you have the instructions and you can see it for yourself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If I tell you that the instructions do not include this, would be opposed to that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik -- please proceed, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the existence of the recommendation of the Serbian Assembly of 11 December 1991, whereby each municipality could establish a Serb municipality if it felt that its population was in danger -- its Serb interests were in danger, rather?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please then look at document number 5. Can you see the recommendation on the establishment?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please read the title of the decision?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The recommendation on the establishment of the Municipal Assemblies of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the date of the issuance of this decision?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "11 December 1991, Sarajevo," in the left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please read out the fourth paragraph of the decision.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not really legible. I will try, but it is quite a poor copy. "The decision on the establishment of the Municipal Assemblies" --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, the paragraph above that one.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The deputies of the Municipal Assemblies of the Serbian people ought to cease their operations within the Municipal Assemblies and their working bodies unless this is contrary to the requirements of the preservation of equality," and I cannot make out this part. "And the interests of the Serbian people," I believe it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, the part that you read, that they should cease operating, rather what it says is that they should continue working?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, that they should continue working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. This particular article, does it correspond to Article 7 of your decision?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are consistent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we go back to document number 1 for a moment -- or rather, can you tell us what does the title of the instructions say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's known to the Chamber. There's no need to ask this to the witness, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It says: "The Serbian Democratic Party." Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please turn to item 6 -- or rather, the document number 6. On page 2, SA009490 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter isn't certain about the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I realise there are logistical difficulties with the entire process; nevertheless, the sooner we get these documents the easier it will be for us to identify the English translations if they exist and the easier it will be for us to assess if there is any need for any additional contextual revision of the questions or any re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand. Mr. Tieger, the Chamber has to find, because it was confronted with the logistical problems last week, the Chamber will certainly pay further attention with how to deal with that. Unfortunately, we could not solve that over the weekend. Some of the documents of course are known, some of the documents we all remember that they were in evidence, such as the agenda item of the -- on the 19th and the 20th of December. But we'll certainly pay specific attention to that. Please proceed, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I truly apologise. I spent the entire night looking for the English translations of these documents, but I was not able to find them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're talking about document number 6, page 2. Can you please read out the title of the document.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The decision on the confirmation of the proclaimed Serbian municipality of Bosanska Krupa."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what the date is.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 11th December 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 1, is it -- has it been sent to the president of the national Assembly, Mr. Momcilo Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say who it was delivered to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 1?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we conclude that this decision was adopted and sent to the president of the Assembly before both the recommendations and the instructions?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Document number 7.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the only document I managed to find an English translation for. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us for the sake of the record what document this is.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document by the Executive Board dated 13th March, 1992 I believe, although I'm not certain about the year, to all the Municipal Boards of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it say "the SDS Executive Board"?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does say the Executive Board of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This -- the Trial Chamber is familiar with this document, so I will not go into it. I will just put a question to you. Can we see that this Executive Board is raising the urgency of some matter here or --what is this document about really?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see the -- it's the establishment of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please quote the title?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "To all the Municipal Boards of the Serbian Democratic Party in accordance with," and I cannot make out this part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- necessary to assess --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, do you have any recollection in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. relation to this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't recall this document, but we must have received it because the mail was coming in regularly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [In English] Sorry, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, your last question was about dates in a Bosanska Krupa document, whether it was prior to or later than the 19th of December. This Chamber is able, if it looks at a document or a decision taken on the 11th of December, that that's prior to the 19th of December. Therefore, there's no need unless this witness would have any specific knowledge about what happened in Bosanska Krupa. So therefore that makes not such sense. It's not to say that you could not draw -- the Defence could not draw the attention to this decision being prior to the 19th of December. But there's no use of asking this witness about it. More or less the same is true for the next one, where the witness has no recollection. So therefore, I'll give you another five minutes to finish.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have five minutes to finish. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only need to select one question. I have several.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at document which is your order on the -- your order proclaiming the War Presidency. That's to be found behind number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krajisnik, I take it that you want to draw the attention of the witness to the decision dated the 16th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a decision -- yes, that's right. Thank you very much for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, you stated that on the 16th of January, 1992, you established the War Presidency. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, but I have to tell you the following. If one document --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. I only have five minutes left. Is that right? I just wanted to hear if that's right.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I saw the document with my signature and stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, the witness may complete his answer. Mr. Prstojevic, if you'd like to add something, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to add the following. If a document does not bear a signature or a stamp, it indicates that this was a draft and was not an official document. However, this particular document was not controversial because we could not convene the session of a Municipal Assembly immediately after the Crisis Staff, so we established a War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tieger wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm trying to clarify whether or not there is any confusion. The witness's previous testimony on more than one occasion was that the Serbian Assembly of Ilidza and the Serbian Crisis Staff were established in January of 1992. I don't know if we're talking about a different body or if the witness is talking about a different year with reference to this particular --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or there's a mistake in the dating of --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct. But if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could ask the witness. Mr. Prstojevic, I said -- in -- Mr. Krajisnik asked you -- Mr. Prstojevic, you stated on the 16th of January, 1992, you established the War Presidency. Now, if you look at this document you'll see that it's dated the 16th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a slip of the tongue because the 16th of January, 1993, is the correct date. There was no such thing in 1992. There were no War Presidencies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krajisnik, this is about War Presidencies, I do understand, and not about Crisis Staffs. What the witness has told us is that this document was not signed. I don't know whether we -- it's not evidence I think until now. So we'd have to look further at this document, unless you would have any specific questions about it at this moment. But the attention is drawn to the fact that it's 1993 rather than 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to ask the witness the following.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you issue the order on the establishment based on the decision of the Serbian Assembly of 11 -- of the -- or rather, of the national Assembly of the 11 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision was taken, as indicated in the heading. However, as the War Presidency ceased to function, we were unable to immediately convene the Municipal Assembly, and that was a problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at the document number 0149-0941. That's the one immediately following your decision. Could you please read the title of the decision.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The decision on the invalidity of the" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to read out slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, could you please read slowly the title of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Decision invalidating the decision on the establishment of the war commissions in the municipalities during a state of war or a state of imminent threat of war."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was the basis of the issuance of this decision?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to Article 80, item 1 -- or rather, paragraph 1, item 7 of the constitution of Republika Srpska, the national Assembly session held on the 17th of December, 1992. That's when it was adopted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the decision pursuant to which you issued your order on the establishment of the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, apparently it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only have one more question left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, are you aware of any document on the basis of which the War Presidency was established in the municipalities or a war commission was established in the municipalities whereby the Crisis Staffs were abolished?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several issues related to this. The Crisis Staffs ceased to exist with the establishment of the war commissions. If you'll remember, they -- at some point during the war, I can't remember when exactly, War Presidencies were established by the state political leadership. Of course you know that after the Dayton Accords the Presidency or the commission of the Serbian town of Sarajevo was established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking about the documents. Can you remember the document on the basis of which war -- municipal War Presidencies were established?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the one in this document dated 16th January?
